independent_initial_proposal.note: Formed from the packet only; lexical citations are from model knowledge and should be checked by a human editor.

Gen.1.1.lexical: רֵאשִׁית (7225) 'beginning/first(fruits)'. בָּרָא qal perf 3ms (OSHB HVqp3ms) with divine subject only in the Hebrew Bible; no material object marked. הַשָּׁמַיִם וְאֵת הָאָרֶץ: a merism for the ordered cosmos.
Gen.1.1.syntactic: Three readings: (A) independent main clause: 'In the beginning God created…'; (B) temporal clause with רֵאשִׁית as construct before a finite verb: 'When God began to create…' — construct before a finite clause is attested (e.g. Hos 1:2 תְּחִלַּת דִּבֶּר; Exod 6:28 בְּיוֹם דִּבֶּר), so the missing article does not exclude it, but also does not prove it: temporal adverbs often lack the article (cf. Isa 46:10 מֵרֵאשִׁית). (C) revocalizing בָּרָא as infinitive בְּרֹא is a reconstruction, NOT the attested MT vocalization in the packet.
Gen.1.1.discourse: 1:1 can function as a heading/summary of the whole 1:1–2:3 unit (compatible with A); 2:4b, by contrast, uses an infinitive (בְּיוֹם עֲשׂוֹת), so 1:1's finite form is at least a different construction. 1:2 opens with waw + subject + qatal (background), which fits A and B equally.
Gen.1.1.textual: No variant in packet. Reported ancient versions (Greek ἐν ἀρχῇ, Latin in principio) render an independent clause — reported, not verified here.
Gen.1.1.reception: Temporal-clause reading is associated with Rashi and Ibn Ezra and modern NJPS/NRSV-note-type translations — commonly reported, not verified in this run.

proposal.en: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.
proposal.es: Al comienzo, Dios creó los cielos y la tierra.
proposal.es_option: En el principio, Dios creó los cielos y la tierra.

Gen.1.2.lexical: תֹהוּ וָבֹהוּ: rhyming pair; תֹהוּ elsewhere 'waste, wilderness, nothingness' (Deut 32:10; Isa 45:18 where it contrasts with 'to be inhabited'; Jer 4:23 echoes the whole pair). So the sense is 'uninhabitable waste and emptiness' more than geometric 'formlessness'. תְהוֹם without article (quasi-proper 'the Deep'). רוּחַ (fem.) = wind / breath / spirit. מְרַחֶפֶת piel ptc fs (OSHB HVprfsa), feminine agreement with רוּחַ; piel elsewhere only Deut 32:11 (eagle over its young).
Gen.1.2.syntactic: Three nominal/background clauses: (1) earth — הָיְתָה qatal after fronted subject = state 'was', not event 'became' (the 'gap' reading needs a wayyiqtol-type sequence the text lacks); (2) darkness over surface of the deep — verbless; (3) ruach + participle = ongoing state 'was hovering'.
Gen.1.2.genitive_test: Definiteness: if אֱלֹהִים is treated as a name, the chain is definite ('the ruach of God'). Counter-test: אִישׁ־אֱלֹהִים without article is used indefinitely ('a man of God', e.g. 1 Sam 2:27). Result: definiteness does not decide 'a' vs 'the'.
Gen.1.2.superlative_test: אֱלֹהִים as superlative ('mighty wind') is possible elsewhere (cf. Jonah 3:3 לֵאלֹהִים), but in Gen 1 אֱלֹהִים is the acting subject in every other occurrence; a superlative here is the weakest of the three readings.

Gen.1.3.lexical_syntactic: וַיֹּאמֶר wayyiqtol; יְהִי qal jussive 3ms (HVqj3ms) — third-person directive; וַיְהִי־אוֹר wayyiqtol of the same root, maqqef-bound. Command/fulfilment pair with identical root and noun.
Gen.1.3.discourse: Under reading A it is the first narrated speech-act after a heading; under reading B it is the main clause of 1:1–3. Its own translation is the same in both cases; only punctuation of 1:1–2 changes.

findings.finding: Packet confirms tipcha on בְּרֵאשִׁית; the earlier zaqef-qatan claims (Claude v0.3.0 round 1, Gemini round 1) are wrong in fact, as GPT round 2 and Gemini round 3 already stated. Even correct accents are medieval reception and do not decide A vs B.

Clause-by-clause tests do not decide wind vs spirit: definiteness is neutral (אִישׁ־אֱלֹהִים 'a man of God'); the piel bird image (Deut 32:11) favors an animate-like agent; the wind-over-waters motif (Gen 8:1 וַיַּעֲבֵר אֱלֹהִים רוּחַ … וַיָּשֹׁכּוּ הַמָּיִם; Exod 14:21) favors wind; superlative reading is weakest. This run therefore does NOT join the pilot's request to flip the text to 'spirit'; it supports keeping the selection with a mandatory note, and records the pilot's opposite judgment as a genuine Claude-to-Claude disagreement.
findings.strength: main unresolved issue; editorial, not textual

findings.finding: 'unformed / 형체 없이 / sin forma' leans toward shapelessness; usage (Isa 45:18, Jer 4:23, Deut 32:10) leans toward 'uninhabitable waste'. Not an error; a note-level nuance. Option: ko '황량하고 텅 비어', en 'a desolate emptiness' / 'waste and void', es 'desolada y vacía'.

'Al comienzo' is correct Spanish; 'En el principio' matches the English pattern and the established Spanish biblical idiom. Three Claude-labelled records (v0.3.0, pilot, this run) prefer it; GPT kept 'Al comienzo'. Optional, stylistic.

strongest_objection_to_own_view: For 1:1 the strongest objection is the missing article plus the logical tension of 1:2: if 1:1 narrates a completed first act, why is the earth then 'waste and void'? Reading 1:1 as a heading answers it, but that is also an interpretation; reading B removes the tension at the cost of a long dependent sentence. For 1:2, the strongest objection to keeping 'wind' is that מְרַחֶפֶת describes a living, bird-like hovering, which a Korean reader hears more naturally of '영' than of '바람'.

final_opinion_ko: 세 절의 현행 채택문에 원문 오역은 없다. 1:1은 독립 도입문(표제적 기능 포함)을 유지하되 시간절 독법(B)을 강한 대안으로 계속 표시하고, 모음 재구성(בְּרֹא)은 증언된 본문이 아닌 재구성으로만 언급해야 한다. 1:2의 רוח אלהים은 절 단위 검사(한정성·최상급·동사 분사·병행 용례)로도 결정되지 않으므로, 이번 실행은 파일럿 Claude 검토의 '영' 전환 요청에 동참하지 않고 현행 '바람' + 필수 주석을 지지한다. 이는 Claude 표지 기록 사이의 실제 이견으로 보존한다. 1:3은 변경 불필요. 선택 사항: 1:1 스페인어 'En el principio', 1:2 תהו의 '황무지' 뉘앙스 주석.
